COASTAL
Three years on, the Cardigan Bay saltmarsh is holding sediment faster than projected.

Six seasons of accretion data from the southern transect now sit comfortably above the original baseline. We break down what worked, what we mis-modeled, and where the next forty hectares are likely to go.

2026-05-04
· DISPATCH
· 6 MIN
Beaver dam analogues at Glen Lowan: first measurable channel widening.

BDA reach C now sits 0.41m above the pre-install thalweg. Sediment lensing visible in three pools. We expected this around month 14; we got it at month 9.

— A. MENDEZ
· COASTAL · BEAVER · MONITORING
2026-04-22
· QUARTERLY
· 11 MIN
From the Cardigan Final Three: Sortie heatmaps of ute grazed Spanish oak under generated protection.

Q1 saw an order of magnitude reduction in browse pressure across the southern parcels. We map the new sortie patterns and what they imply for fencing decisions next quarter.

— L. ORTIZ
· QUARTERLY · GRAZING · DATA
2026-04-10
· FIELD ENTRY
· 8 MIN
Year-three vertical audit, Loch Awe planting: 78.4% across 311,000 stems.

Survival rates from the third-year audit. Caledonian pine outperformed in the windward parcels; birch underperformed on the southern aspect, as last year's note predicted.

— R. FORBES
· FORESTRY · ANNUAL · AUDIT
2026-03-28
· FINANCE
· 5 MIN
Donation reconciliation, August 2025: 2,114 contributions matched, 14 pending review.

Our reconciliation pass on August traffic. Most of the residue is wire-transfer ledger entries that won't resolve until the bank closes its quarter. Detail below.

— C. WHELAN
· FINANCE · OPERATIONS
2026-03-12
· RESEARCH
· 9 MIN
Peat re-wetting at Borden Mires: water table holding within 4 cm of surface for 142 of 158 monitored days.

Borden has been our test of how shallow drains, blocked aggressively, behave on shoulder seasons. The data is unusually clean — and unusually flattering to the cheap plug method.

— P. NWANKWO
· PEAT · HYDROLOGY · RESEARCH
